description.narrative: The activities proposed, particularly those under “planning for durable solutions”, are intended both to secure tangible peace dividends for target communities as well as to function as catalytic inputs for peace and stability in Sudan

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
UNDP as the Implementing Partner will comply with the policies, procedures and practices of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS.)

5 awareness campaigns on women rights held - A community-based organization, the Darfur IDP Womens Protection Network, was engaged and conducted awareness-raising campaigns on leadership skills, legal reform, and womens rights, including international and regional treaties (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women - CEDAW; African Protocol for Women). The event was held on 05 August and attended by 202 participants (131 women; 85 youth) in Beida, A similar campaign was Held in Seleah, Manjura, Gozminno. Aburemail, and Falco attended by 209 participants (153 women; 70 70 youth). Four (4) women centres constructed in Seleah, Manjura, Aburemail, and Gozminno to enhance leadership skills and discuss women rights and regional treaties. 9 CSOs trained (56% women CSOs) on human rights-based approaches and programming strengthened

One action plan developed 5 land cases were received in Maala, Silea, Fajola and Jamila villages and all these land conflict cases were successfully resolved to the satisfaction of the parties involved Two sustainable and eco-friendly area-based plans designed 80% men, 20% women 47% youth included in the plan development process. 4 traditional authorities linked to formal governance structures for support and accountability 4 institutions (state and non-state actors) whose capacities are built and functioning successfully One Police Post was established at Aburumel village, and one Prosecutor Office complex was established at Silea village. 105 SPF (92 M, 13 F) were trained on land law reform; how to conduct community patrols, intelligence-led policing, and early warning and early response; tactical intervention and first responder training; how to run the Digital Control Room; on criminal investigation, women and child protection One District court was established in Silea village which is central and accessible by all villages and 24 participants (2 F, 22 M), from judges, prosecutors, Police investigators, and psychosocial workers were trained on fair trail standards, and Sudanese Child Act including drafting a law on combating violence against women 12 CBRMs with 180 members (33 women, 51 youth, 43 nomads) established and functional in Masteri, Terbaibah, Beida, Shushta, Mirmata, Kulkuta Haraza, Tirti, Sileah Manjura, Aburmail, Falco villages. 100% - 11 cases were reported to CBRMs in Jabalmoon and all were successfully resolved at community level to the satisfaction of the parties involved. The case reported included 5 land cases, 2 sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) cases and 4 social cases related to divorces and theft. These cases were reported in Maala, Silea, Fajola, Gozmino, Arja, and Jamila villages by 6 males and 5 females (inclusive of 3 youths) 100% of CBMs stated increase in interactions and communication with other peacebuilding, rule of law and justice institutions at community, locality and state levels; 100% of community members stated increase in access to CBRMs for resolution of conflicts.
